items.issues: Clear 'But let us…keep aloof' pivot; D's 'rejecting all influence' contradicts 'preserve this influence'. Clean.
A/D misread the promise (delay is involuntary); C has no textual basis. Clean.
Abstract philosophical prose raises reading load above easy; D's 'conclusion about criticism' matches final clause. A plausible but text explicitly says no evidence can be produced.
'quite gently', 'drenched and bubbling' + 'So far there was no great harm' support A; D contradicted by 'to make things worse'. Clean.
Final sentence states B almost verbatim. 'squire' vs 'senator' naming is inconsistent in the passage but does not affect answer.
'Welcome, kindred glooms! Congenial horrors, hail!' makes C explicit; 'joyous Spring' may tempt A but speaker is 'Pleased' throughout winter. Clean.

'I have scorned such wisdom' could be read as defiant pride (A); but 'native satisfaction', 'truly wise', 'careful gladness' frame what he rejected as valuable, so D is better. A is a borderline-defensible distractor.
'soft side of a plank', 'sweeten things' are plainly ironic; B is the literal-reading trap. Clean.
Two-part attitude (awe + self-conscious 'tedious') is only captured by B. Clean.
Flatland satire; C correctly frames it as the narrator's explanation. A overreads first sentence, D inverts the comparison. Content is misogynistic in-world satire — flag for sensitivity review.

D is the only option with abstract/interpretive wording while A–C are concrete literal misreadings, making it stand out formally. Passage has a fragment ('The real reason.') that looks like a truncation.
'no evidence…of the recent little revolution', 'carefully rewound' support A; B/C/D each contradict a stated detail. Clean.
Requires synthesizing mirror analogy + parent sentence + alcohol warning; B fits. D misreads the analogy (mind, not body). Slightly above easy.

C is the generic 'record observations' answer and A/B/D have no textual basis, so distractors are weak. Passage has an apparent OCR error ('three quarters of an inch in length', 'swollen one' for the smaller fort).
D is correct and clear; A and C are short literal distortions, B is a fabricated detail. D and B are notably longer than A/C.
Stated explicitly in text; near-lookup. D contradicted (he openly says he lived in Germany). Clean but very easy.
D clearly supported ('she was gone… affright'). B has slight textual hook (nurses as enemies) but hiding is not implied. A is noticeably longer than B/C.
Text directly lists the weed/trout and two-fish scenarios as management problems; B conflates the separate 'bright flies' point. Clean.
'militant Democracy', 'outvote…counteract' support B; C inverts 'not more than we need him'. Clean.
